name: Question 5
problem:
The triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz
$$

is defined over the type II region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le z,\,2\le z\le 3,\,-y-z\le x\le {y}^{2}+{z}^{4}\}.
$$

What is $a+b?$
worked_solution:
A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(y,z)\le x\le {u}_{2}(y,z)\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/a905e1f60fb0aa865c071fcbccbfecb30dcac7a74b4b647d24a40f4c89ff1935.png)

 

If $R$ is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(y,z)=-y-z,\,{u}_{2}(y,z)={y}^{2}+{z}^{4}.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-y-z}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{4}}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le z,\,2\le z\le 3\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-y-z}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{4}}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{z}[{\int }_{-y-z}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{4}}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dy\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{z}{\int }_{-y-z}^{{y}^{2}+{z}^{4}}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=-2+z=z-2.
$$

Question 5
?

The triple integral ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫∗∗∫ab∫∗∗f(x,y,z)dxdydz is defined over the type II region R, given by R={(x,y,z):−2≤y≤z,2≤z≤3,−y−z≤x≤y2+z4}. What is a+b?

a
y2+z4+y+z
b
5
c
y2+z4−y−z
d
z−2
e
z+3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,u1(y,z)≤x≤u2(y,z)}.

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If R is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of f(x,y,z) over R as a mixed integral, as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dx]dA

In our case, we have

u1(y,z)=−y−z,u2(y,z)=y2+z4.

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫−y−zy2+z4f(x,y,z)dx]dA.

Now, the region D is given by D={(x,y):−2≤y≤z,2≤z≤3}.

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over D as a repeated integral, we get ∬D[∫−y−zy2+z4f(x,y,z)dx]dA=∫23∫−2z[∫−y−zy2+z4f(x,y,z)dx]dydz=∫23∫−2z∫−y−zy2+z4f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

Finally, a+b=−2+z=z−2.
